tool_contracts.name: record_changed_paths
tool_contracts.description: After saving an edit batch, immediately record its repository-relative paths and wake the mcp --watch indexer, even during initial indexing. Returns a min_revision receipt for repo_overview or verify_change. This declares saved changes; it does not edit files, expand scan scope, or prove coverage.

paths.description:
One to 128 saved repo-relative paths; deleted paths and directories are valid.
Use "." for the whole repository. Absolute paths and traversal are rejected.

Freshness.description:
Freshness contract attached to graph-sensitive responses. The load-bearing invariant
of the online daemon: a query always reads the latest published snapshot immediately,
but is told when the daemon has observed newer changes than that snapshot represents.

consistency_satisfied.description:
True if this response satisfied the requested `min_revision`/consistency (always
true for `latest_available`/`allow_stale` with no `min_revision`).

dirty_path_count.description:
Total number of paths observed changed since the snapshot (even if the list below
is capped).

dirty_paths.description: Capped sample of dirty paths, for response-size safety.

generated_at_unix_ms.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch when the snapshot was generated.

indexed_revision.description: Highest repository revision represented by the published snapshot.

is_stale.description:
True when `observed_revision > indexed_revision`, or a requested `min_revision`
was not satisfied within the wait budget.

observed_revision.description: Highest revision observed through filesystem events or explicit edit receipts.

rebuilding.description: True when a rebuild is in flight right now.

revision.description: Alias for `indexed_revision` — the revision this answer's snapshot represents.

min_revision.description: Pass this floor to repo_overview or verify_change before using post-edit results.

tool_contracts.name: verify_change
tool_contracts.description: Post-edit check scoped to your paths (or observed dirty paths when empty). After saving, call record_changed_paths and pass its min_revision with wait_ms to wait for the corresponding index. Reports baseline comparability, regressions/fixes and explicit freshness when a requested revision is not ready.

min_revision.description: Revision returned by record_changed_paths after saving the edit batch.

paths.description:
Repo-relative paths the agent touched. Empty means "use the paths the
daemon observed as changed since the snapshot" (`mcp --watch`).

wait_ms.description: Wait budget for that revision, bounded to 120 seconds.

outputSchema.description:
Post-edit answer: did *my* change make things worse, scoped to the touched
paths — not a whole-repo convergence dump.

baseline.description: Identity and comparability of the artifact baseline used for this delta.

fixes.description: resolved + improved findings touching the scope (capped).

guard_verdict.description: Overall guard verdict for the current run (context, not scoped).

honesty.description: Caveats the agent must not miss (e.g. edits the analysis has not seen).

regressions.description: new + worsened findings touching the scope, severity-first (capped).

scope_path_count.description: Total effective scope before the display cap; absent in older responses.

scope_paths.description: Effective scope the delta was computed over (repo-relative, capped).

outputSchema.title: VerifyChangeOutput

comparison.normalization: Complete arrays/order retained; sorted object keys; known root/output prefix substitutions; freshness and work fields kept separately in raw receipts. Additional exact listed metadata paths differ because these are different engine builds/root directories/generation times.

limitations: Measured normal saved-edit receipt flow on two controlled real Draivix file updates, not every watcher/capture failure or interleaving.
Expected initial indexing response is not a parser failure, failed source analysis or transport crash.
Revision-specific failure/retry logic and invalid-input/large-scope behavior have written regression cases but were not executed under the test stop.
Receipts declare saved paths and invalidate a running indexer; they do not edit files, expand scan scope, verify each path is analyzed, certify content hashes or provide durable edit transactions.
All successful source states retain incomplete parser/secondary coverage and an unavailable baseline; zero regressions or fixes is not a clean-code verdict.
Eighteen complete captured data-view comparisons preserve array contents/order and exclude only documented metadata, not a full raw semantic graph comparison.
Final source copy and preserved capture match the common 23,296-file inventory; original Draivix was not written. Intermediate states are declared combinations, not whole historical checkouts.
Times are individual observations on a shared host, not latency guarantees.
The final binary was replayed after production changes; earlier sessions are preserved separately and do not substitute for the final run.
Approved CI, adversarial/concurrent scenarios, stable capture and overall Q01-Q12 acceptance remain open.
